newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia working days lost from disputes rise.
newsitem.headline: Australia working days lost from disputes rise.

text.p: The number of working days lost in Australia through industrial disputes increased to 47,100 in March, up from 17,600 a month earlier, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Friday.
The number of disputes fell to 35 from 36, but the number of employees involved more than doubled, to 34,800 from 17,300.
The bureau said the number of working days lost was the highest since 122,900 days lost in August, 1996.
Education, health and community services, which lost 33,600 days in the month, was the worst-hit sector. Queensland was the worst-hit state, losing 22,500 days in the month.
The bureau said 863,700 working days were lost in the year to March, 274,300 days more than the preceding 12 months.
The construction industry lost the most number of days through the year, with 340,800, ahead of education, health and community services with 200,000 and coal mining, 150,000.
